implementation: Feasible with automatic recovery bounded to a successfully confirmed approve action, which addresses the observed interruption. Before broadcast, an awaited Engine persistPrepared callback atomically attaches exact signature, signed bytes/hash, blockhash, last-valid height, kind and canonical handle to the durable pendingIntent containing request id, fingerprint, actor, scenario, before and intendedAfter. Reconcile uses the same Engine queue as actions and never signs or sends. Fetch getTransaction with base64 encoding and confirmed commitment through paced transport: require metadata success, a valid slot, exact full signed-byte equality and verified signatures. Require the configured approving actor as fee payer/signer and exactly one expected Kontor approve instruction plus the validated compute-unit-limit instruction. Reconstruct its expected compiled message with the saved blockhash/fee payer instead of comparing deserialized writability, because compiled privileges are shared. Bind instruction tag, revision, config, obligation and revision account to canonical derivation. Read canonical state at minContextSlot >= transaction slot; require the exact intended approval-mask delta, unchanged revision/amount/mint/recipient/documents, valid approval expiry and paid=false. Validate intendedAfter contains only the legal approval delta and its one original evidence event, with no settlement or unrelated mutation. Reuse existing link validation. Atomically save verified intendedAfter, real proof, original event IDs, request id/fingerprint idempotency and cleared pendingIntent in one state-file replacement. Repeated checks/restart return that same committed record. Missing, ambiguous, unsuccessful, expired-readiness or unsupported outcomes remain locked. Credit, pay, reset, capture and expected-failure replay recovery remain explicitly operator-assisted. Legacy binding is a separate controller-attested migration, never falsely described as pre-submission capture.
risks: The prepared callback must durably update the exact existing pendingIntent before any send. A write failure aborts broadcast. Public recovery metadata must exclude keys, signed transaction bytes and internal intended snapshots; user-supplied signatures and error-message parsing are never recovery authority.

Read-only inspectPrepared must use raw base64 getTransaction, exact byte/hash/signature comparison and metadata err === null. Null, unconfirmed, missing metadata, RPC errors and 429 exhaustion remain unresolved. No status result can trigger signing, resend, blockhash replacement or another sendTransaction call.

Validate canonical account derivation and independently reconstructed approve instruction/message, not only saved bytes against themselves. Permit only the known compute-unit-limit instruction and one approve instruction; reject extra transfers, foreign programs, wrong actors, wrong obligation/revision and ambiguous transaction versions.

Require the canonical state to equal exactly the saved intended approval transition, not merely contain the target bit: the pending actor was not already approved, exactly its configured bit was added, revision and documents are unchanged, and paid remains false. Additional later approval/revision/payment or expired approval readiness remains conservatively unsupported.

Approve recovery must preserve amount, mint, recipient, original/credit digests and unpaid status. Its exact permitted instruction accounts contain no token-moving vault/recipient inputs and no token transfer instruction; it cannot substantiate payment. Fees remain distinct from Test USD movement.

Validate intendedAfter against the legal before/action approval delta: one matching approval, one original approval evidence event, correct readiness status and only the existing engine second-approval previousInstruction behavior. Preserve all prior evidence prefixes and IDs, invoice/credit fields and settlement=null; reject unrelated changes. Commit state, request-id/fingerprint idempotency and pending removal together. Auxiliary-proof failure cannot clear the authoritative lock.

For the existing interruption, a controller may attach a uniquely verified historical journal to an already durable matching pendingIntent only after exact instruction/action/actor/obligation/revision/time and successful chain evidence agree. Record this as controller-attested legacy binding with evidence and backup. If original intent is absent, candidate journals conflict or identity cannot be established, do not fabricate intent or use the error string; retain the lock and disclose operator assistance.

Automatic recovery is approval-only. Credit, payment, reset, capture and expected-failed stale replay remain operator-assisted with action-specific honest UI text. Failed transactions are not unlocked for retries. Broader recovery needs separately accepted engineering scope; no generic successful signature may unlock an unsupported operation.

This is user-authorized recovery cycle 3 under the same shared $10 ceiling; cycle 4 requires actual remaining findings. Fresh-context browser evidence is non-isolated usability evidence, separate from source-aware transaction proof. No program or ledger-authority change is needed.
taskSplit: After PM final acceptance, parent owns the Engine pendingIntent/prepared callback, serialized reconcile operation, atomic idempotent state commit, exact server-side action verifier, read-only endpoint and public recovery contract. Parent retains sole control-plane and legacy-migration authority.

After PM acceptance, SDE client builder adds a small read-only inspectPrepared surface using queued base64 getTransaction and minContextSlot account reads; it has no path to signed, submit or broadcast. Existing paced transport and signature-preservation tests remain mandatory.

Independent integration tester verifies exact successful approval recovery, no send/sign calls, repeated checks/restart/crash idempotency, wrong-byte/hash/signature/action/actor/account/revision rejection, extra-instruction rejection, illegal intendedAfter mutations, later-state ambiguity and failed/unseen/unconfirmed/rate-limit lock retention. Include compiled-message privilege normalization and explicit unsupported-operation cases.

UX builder implements operation-specific actor/amount guidance, one wrapping technical identifier disclosure, visible non-overlapping checking/last-result state and unresolved evidence separate from completed records. No transaction retry or unlock button is introduced.

Parent first reconciles the already-stuck obligation through the independently verified legacy binding when available, preserving its recorded intent and evidence, then runs typecheck/build and fresh-context desktop/390 px recovery review. No extra payment/reset is needed solely for recovery layout tests.
